subject.title: fix(exec): require approval for Windows shell expansions

question: Should Windows PowerShell expansion commands be admitted into exec analysis only as one-shot explicit approvals, even when an existing exact-command durable approval matches?
rationale: This is a security and compatibility policy choice: the patch fixes a real Windows approval-analysis gap, but it intentionally makes some previously reusable approvals prompt every time.

options.title: Accept One-Shot Expansion Approvals
options.body: Approve the security posture that PowerShell expansion tokens can be parsed for review but never converted into reusable allow-always approvals.

options.title: Require Stronger Live Edge Proof
options.body: Ask for a Windows live run showing the durable exact-command trust case still returns approval-pending before merge.

options.title: Pause For Reusable Trust Semantics
options.body: Pause the PR if maintainers want exact-command durable trust to remain valid for expansion-bearing commands and redesign the approval model first.

recommendation.title: Accept One-Shot Expansion Approvals
recommendation.body: Approve the security posture that PowerShell expansion tokens can be parsed for review but never converted into reusable allow-always approvals.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits on the command planner and durable approval semantics introduced in the Tree-sitter command authorization work.
